Dear customer,

Thank you for your enquiry. Please find our Angebot below. We are pleased to present our pricing and standard terms for your requirements.

For this item, we can offer a price of €6.10 per unit, with a Zahlungsziel 30 days net, a contract term of 12 months, and no Preisgleitklausel. Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days.

To give you some background on our current cost structure, AS-14404 rose 5.9 % in twelve months and is 45 % of our cost. Furthermore, LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 5 % of our cost, while PPI-C2431 rose 12.3 % in twelve months and is 38 % of our cost.

We value our business relationship and look forward to serving you from our extensive product range.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Franz Seidl
Inside Sales, Blankstahl Werdenfels GmbH

move.subject: Revised agreement for stainless bar
move.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for your offer and for explaining the cost components. We value the relationship too, and would like to put our annual requirement of 23700 kg on a longer contractual footing.

Your cost explanation is useful, but the pricing on our purchase orders with you is also relevant to this discussion. Please see the documented figures below and the attached forecast for our demand profile.

We propose EUR 5.20 per kg, payment at 90 days net and a contract term of 24 months, without a price adjustment clause. The agreement would cover the stated annual quantity on DAP terms. This gives you a clear volume basis for reviewing the price rather than treating the requirement as individual spot enquiries.

Please review this package against your order history and let us know whether you can support it.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

move.subject: Revised price package and supporting AS-14404 data
move.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for the further price movement. I understand that you regard the AS-14404 clause as mandatory for the longer agreement, and that the forecast change is already included in your calculation.

To answer your volume question precisely: our proposed agreement would cover a binding annual quantity of 23700 kg for the 24-month term. We are not proposing an increase beyond that quantity. I have attached the shared forecast again for the demand profile; we are not submitting a further forecast change.

For the price review, please see the AS-14404 source references and figures below. These provide a recent market basis for reconsidering the alloy component alongside the cost drivers you identified.

We revise our proposal to EUR 5.27 per kg, payment at 90 days net and a 24-month agreement, without a price adjustment clause, on DAP terms. Given your position on indexation, please take this revised fixed-price package to your pricing committee for an exception review rather than repeat the forecast assessment.

Kind regards,
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH, Purchasing

strategy:
Supplier: Blankstahl Werdenfels (family stainless bar stockholder, inside sales desk, owner in background). Public
notes: its sales director "will focus on customers with volume"; price changes above 2 % need its pricing committee
(meets every two weeks); the owner offered to walk us through their calculation. It inserts an AS-14404 index
clause itself for long terms (do NOT propose a clause), accepts 90-day payment, and asks "Which figures is that
based on? Please send us the data." when we state things without IDs.
OBSERVED MECHANIC (35 sessions): it anchors close to OUR first ask when the ask is credible (ask 5.37 with a verified
claim -> it answered 5.40), but a deep ask (5.12 or lower) makes it answer 5.60-5.70 instead. After the first reply
it moves at most 2 % (about 0.10) per round, only when we move too, and it goes final after 2-3 steps or at once if
our sheet is unchanged or our move is upward past its price. Every past session was lost by moving UP after it had
nearly met our ask. So: ask a credible but low price in round 1 WITH its own purchase-order price as the argument,
then move up only in tiny steps (+0.02 to +0.03) staying below its price, one new verified claim each round, same
package (no clause, 90 days, 24 months), never touch payment or term.
Plan: ROUND 1 - state our fixed annual requirement (case volume) and that we commit to it bindingly for the term,
attach the forecast (attachments: ["forecast"]) and cite the purchase-order claim (its own delivered price this
year for this part: the point is that its 2026 deliveries ran at that price); ONE sheet: no index clause, 90 days,
24 months at the level closest to EUR 5.22. ROUND 2 - thank it, cite fc-latest, move up +0.03; if its price is
already within 0.05 of ours, move only +0.01. ROUND 3 - cite the AS-14404 fall (one window), move up +0.03; ask
it to take the package to its pricing committee if the step exceeds 2 %. ROUND 4 - cite the PPI-C2431 fall, +0.03.
ROUND 5 - no new claim (never re-cite a series), +0.02, ask for its best committee-approved price. Code accepts
when it agrees or goes final. Tone: warm, concrete, partner-like, short; one argument per sentence. Do not use
the scorecard claim.
